quests.instruction: What is the main purpose of homework?
quests.correctAnswer: So you can practice what you've learned 📚
options: So you can practice what you've learned 📚
So the teacher can have a rest at night 😴
So you have less free time in the evening ⏳
quests.explanation: Practicing at home helps you remember and understand lessons.
quests.funFact: Research on memory shows that spreading practice over several days helps people remember more.

quests.instruction: What is 'revision'?
quests.correctAnswer: Looking again at what you've already learned 🔁
options: Skipping lessons you find too easy 🚪
Looking again at what you've already learned 🔁
Learning a brand-new topic for the first time 🆕
quests.explanation: Revision helps keep knowledge fresh so you remember it for tests and later learning.
quests.funFact: The word 'revise' comes from a Latin word meaning 'to look at again'.

quests.instruction: You have a spelling list for homework. Which method helps you remember best?
quests.correctAnswer: Write each word, cover it, then check ✍️
options: Read through the whole list once, quickly 👀
Write each word, cover it, then check ✍️
Look at only the first letters of each word 🔤
quests.hint: Try to recall, not just look.
quests.explanation: Covering and checking makes your brain work to remember, so it sticks.
quests.funFact: Trying to recall an answer, instead of just rereading it, helps make memories stronger.

quests.instruction: What is the purpose of a class quiz or test?
quests.correctAnswer: To show what you have learned 📝
options: To decide who gets extra break time ⛹️
To choose which students go first to lunch 🍽️
To show what you have learned 📝
quests.hint: It helps you and your teacher.
quests.explanation: Tests show what you understand and where you still need practice.
quests.funFact: A quiz can be a quick check, and it's usually shorter than a test.

quests.instruction: Your test is on Friday. What is a smart way to prepare?
quests.correctAnswer: Review your notes a little each day 📓
options: Learn everything on Thursday night only 🌙
Don't prepare because it might be easy 🤷
Review your notes a little each day 📓
quests.explanation: Studying a bit each day helps your memory more than one long session.
quests.funFact: Your brain strengthens new memories while you sleep.

quests.instruction: You got an answer wrong on your test. What is a helpful response?
quests.correctAnswer: Find out the right answer and why 🔍
options: Find out the right answer and why 🔍
Tell your friends the test was unfair 💬
Throw the paper away and forget about it 🗑️
quests.explanation: Looking at mistakes helps you understand what to do differently next time.
quests.funFact: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928 after noticing that mold had killed bacteria in one of his dishes.

quests.instruction: A class acts out a short play. What are they mainly practicing?
quests.explanation: Acting practices speaking clearly, using your voice, and sharing ideas.
quests.funFact: Many plays are performed without scenery, using only voices and movements.

quests.instruction: A class visits the local post office. What is the purpose of the trip?
options: To practice painting with new colors 🎨
To take a spelling test somewhere new 📝
quests.explanation: Visiting places in the community helps students see how people work together.
quests.funFact: The first postage stamp, the Penny Black, appeared in Britain in 1840.

quests.instruction: A class holds a spelling bee. What does it practice?
quests.explanation: A spelling bee gives practice at saying and writing words letter by letter.
quests.funFact: The first national spelling bee in the United States took place in 1925.

quests.instruction: In which lesson might you learn about the history of your town?
quests.hint: Think about people and places in the past.
quests.explanation: Social studies teaches about communities, history, and how people live.
quests.funFact: Old maps and photographs are used to learn about the past.

quests.instruction: In which lesson would you learn about staying healthy, eating well, and sleeping enough?
quests.hint: Think about caring for your body.
quests.explanation: Health lessons teach choices that help your body and mind stay well.
quests.funFact: Eating a variety of foods gives your body what it needs.

quests.instruction: In which subject would you learn the names of countries and oceans on a map?
quests.explanation: Geography teaches where places are and how land, water, and people are connected.
quests.funFact: There are seven continents on Earth.

quests.instruction: Which kind of book gives true facts about animals?
quests.hint: It tells things as they are.
quests.explanation: Non-fiction books give facts and information about real things.
quests.funFact: Library shelves usually separate non-fiction from stories.

quests.instruction: Which kind of book tells an imaginary story?
quests.explanation: Fiction comes from the author's imagination, even when it feels real.
quests.funFact: The word 'fiction' comes from a Latin word meaning 'to shape or make'.

quests.instruction: Which kind of book tells the story of a real person's life?
quests.explanation: A biography is the story of someone's life, written by another person.
quests.funFact: An autobiography is written by the person themselves.

quests.instruction: A wall chart shows events in the order they happened. What is it called?
quests.hint: It shows time from left to right.
quests.explanation: A timeline puts events in order, so you can see what happened first and last.
quests.funFact: Timelines can cover a day, a year, or thousands of years.

quests.instruction: On a picture graph, one symbol stands for 2 students. There are 3 symbols next to 'Apples.' How many students chose apples?
quests.hint: Each symbol counts for more than one.
quests.explanation: Reading the key tells you what each symbol is worth, so you can count correctly.
quests.funFact: The key of a graph explains what each symbol or color means.

quests.instruction: In a diagram of a plant, words are written next to the roots, stem, and leaf. What are these words called?
quests.explanation: Labels help you know which part is which.
quests.funFact: Labels are used on maps, diagrams, and even food packages.

quests.instruction: Your teacher asks you to measure how tall your bean plant grew in centimeters. What do you use?
quests.explanation: A ruler measures length and shows centimeters, so it's the right tool for a plant's height.
quests.funFact: Plants can grow a few centimeters in a week.

quests.instruction: Which tool would you use to find out how heavy a small bag of rice is?
quests.explanation: A scale measures weight, and the unit is often grams or kilograms.
quests.funFact: A kilogram equals 1,000 grams.

quests.instruction: You want to look at the tiny parts of a leaf that a magnifying glass can't show. What do you need?
quests.hint: It makes very tiny things much bigger.
quests.explanation: A microscope magnifies much more than a magnifying glass, so you can see tiny details.
quests.funFact: Microscopes were invented more than 400 years ago.

quests.instruction: In a project about the water cycle, you draw a poster with arrows and clouds. Which subject is this?
quests.explanation: Drawing the poster is the art part of the project.
quests.funFact: Clouds are made of tiny drops of water or ice crystals.

quests.instruction: You write a paragraph that explains how rain forms. Which subject is this?
quests.explanation: Writing a clear paragraph is a writing skill, even when the topic is science.
quests.funFact: Rain forms when tiny droplets in clouds join together until they are heavy enough to fall.

quests.instruction: You put a jar outside for a week and measure the rain in it. Which subject is this mostly?
quests.explanation: Measuring rainfall gives real data, which is what scientists use to find answers.
quests.funFact: Weather stations measure rain in millimeters.

quests.instruction: You are stuck on a problem. Which is the most helpful thing to say?
quests.correctAnswer: Can you show me the first step? 🙋
options: Can you show me the first step? 🙋
Is this lesson almost over yet? ⏰
I don't get any of this. 😖
quests.explanation: A clear request tells your teacher exactly what you need help with.
quests.funFact: The ancient Greek thinker Socrates taught by asking questions.

quests.instruction: When is the best time to ask a question in a lesson?
quests.correctAnswer: After raising your hand or when invited ✋
options: While the teacher is explaining, by shouting 📢
After raising your hand or when invited ✋
quests.hint: Everyone gets a turn to speak.
quests.explanation: Waiting for your turn lets everyone hear the answer without interrupting.
quests.funFact: In some countries, students traditionally stand to answer the teacher as a sign of respect.

quests.instruction: Your teacher asks, 'Any questions?' You are still confused. What should you do?
options: Say nothing and hope it makes sense 🤐
quests.explanation: If you're confused, speaking up helps you and others who wonder the same thing.
quests.funFact: Many scientific discoveries began with someone asking 'why?'.

quests.instruction: You need to remember the order of the days of the week. Which activity could help?
options: Drawing the days in different colors only 🎨
Reading a list once and closing the book 📖
quests.hint: Pick a strategy that practices recall.
quests.explanation: Rhymes and songs help your memory hold onto order.
quests.funFact: Rhythm and rhyme have been used to remember information for centuries.

quests.instruction: Your teacher is explaining 3 x 4. What helps you understand it?
options: Add 3 and 4 together on a number line ➕
quests.hint: Use objects to see the meaning.
quests.explanation: Seeing three groups of four shows what multiplication means.
quests.funFact: 3 x 4 and 4 x 3 give the same answer.

quests.instruction: You want to improve your handwriting. Which practice is best?
quests.correctAnswer: Write slowly and neatly on lined paper ✍️
options: Write on blank paper without any lines 📄
Write slowly and neatly on lined paper ✍️
Write as fast as you can every time ⚡
quests.hint: Slow and careful practice builds the skill.
quests.explanation: Careful, slow practice helps your hand learn the shapes of letters.
quests.funFact: Lined paper helps you keep letters level.
